conventions.convention: The root inner product is linear first; |x><y| sends z to <z,y>root x.
Controlled operators use control-first order: C(U)=diag(I_H,U). Controlled access and its cost must be explicitly granted.
Inverse availability and cost are separate from forward and controlled access. A chronological list is inverted by reversing it and taking adjoints; the empty list denotes identity.
Relative phase is the unit-modulus part of β/α for an ordered orthonormal pair, and is undefined if either coordinate vanishes.
CP(θ)=diag(1,1,1,exp(iθ)) in basis 00,01,10,11. Pθ=exp(iθ/2)Rz(θ), so controlling Rz alone omits a control phase.
CNOT uses the first wire as control and second as target: (a,t) maps to (a,t XOR a).
Multi-control activation uses m≥1 disjoint control wires and activates exactly on the specified string s. Negative controls are conjugated by X on the zero positions of s.
Entanglement is failure to be a product ray across a specified ordered tensor cut with nonzero factors; Schmidt rank is coefficient-matrix rank.
RΠ=2Π−I is positive on the projection range; SΠ=I−2Π=−RΠ. Their controlled forms differ by control Z. A conjugated reflection includes preparation, reflection, and inverse-preparation costs.
The controlled-global-phase witness requires a nonzero finite-dimensional complex target and separately granted controlled access to both U and exp(iθ)U; witness preparation is not assumed free.

load_bearing.statement: For a control qubit C and finite-dimensional complex target H with unitary U, define C(U)=diag(I_H,U) on C⊗H. Controlled access explicitly grants this block operation; ordinary black-box access does not silently grant it or assign its cost.

For an orthogonal projection Π on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, RΠ=2Π−I and SΠ=I−2Π=−RΠ. Direct and controlled reflection access require explicit declarations; implementing a prepared-state reflection as UR0U† includes all three calls.

For an orthogonal projection Π on a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, RΠ and SΠ are self-adjoint unitary involutions. They have opposite signs on range and kernel, and C(SΠ)=Z_C C(RΠ), where Z_C=diag(I_H,−I_H).

For a unit vector u in a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with the root pairing linear first, P_u=|u><u| is self-adjoint, idempotent, has one-dimensional range, is non-negative, and has trace one. In particular it is a density operator.

For unitary U on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex target and real θ, assume separate controlled access to U and exp(iθ)U. Choose a unit eigenvector φ with eigenvalue μ and prepare control (|0>+conjugate(μ)|1>)/√2. The plus-control outcome has probabilities 1 and cos²(θ/2), respectively. The outcome laws differ exactly when θ is not in 2πZ; otherwise the controlled maps coincide. Access and preparation are not asserted free.
In basis 00,01,10,11, CNOT with first wire control and second wire target sends |a,t> to |a,t XOR a>, equivalently C(X)=diag(I,X).

Across nonzero finite-dimensional complex factors H_A⊗H_B, a pure state is entangled when its ray contains no nonzero decomposable vector. Schmidt rank is coefficient-matrix rank, independent of ordered orthonormal product basis, and equals the number of positive terms in every Schmidt decomposition. Entanglement is equivalent to Schmidt rank exceeding one.

seams_checked.note: Dirac pairing reversal and outer-product coordinates preserve the root linear-first convention.
Uses finite POVMs on nonzero spaces and trace-defined probabilities; witness effects are verified locally.
Ray, density, and Schmidt interfaces are used with their stated domains and coefficient conjugation.
Exact X, Z, H, and Rz signs and scalar phases are retained.
Ordered product bases, tensor maps, and product pairings agree; finite target bases are supplied where needed.
CNOT order, inverse chronology, explicit controlled oracle access, and the phase witness are stated faithfully.
Uses exact CP action, ordered CNOT, reversed adjoint lists, and the outer-control phase caveat.
Separates supplied controlled powers from repeated C(U) calls and charges inverse powers separately.
Reflection signs and prepared-reflection costs agree; unit-vector density use is qualified.
Uses S-sign reflections, retains controlled scalar phases, and explicitly supplies enlarged reflections and inverses.
Retains the signed iterate and separately supplied controlled/inverse operations.
Uses plus-on-range reflections and distinguishes standalone phase invariance from controlled eigenphase behavior.
Range reflections use preparation–reflection–inverse preparation; controlled constituents and costs are explicit.
Stored-data access uses identity/operation controlled blocks and reverses the full circuit for inverses.
Hamiltonian access keeps controlled and inverse capabilities and their costs explicit.
Term-list and simulation contracts grant neither controlled nor inverse access implicitly.
Explicitly identifies its R0=I−2Π0 as the supplier's S sign and charges the control-Z sign correction.
Forward, inverse, controlled, controlled-inverse, and SELECT operations remain separate supplied capabilities.
Relative phase is undefined at zero coordinates; the displayed Z phase multiplies β/α by exp(−2iφ).
Projector phases use plus-on-range reflections and the exact control-Z correction for the opposite sign.
Signal-sequence reflection signs agree, with inverse/control/reflection access separately costed.
Capped amplification treats inverse calls as separately supplied and chargeable.
Finite-cap amplification explicitly supplies S-sign reflections, inverse preparation, and controlled operations.
Spectral access separately supplies and charges preparation, controlled powers, and inverse operations.
Coherent sampling grants forward, inverse, and controlled calls separately; unit-vector density use is faithful.
Capped-amplification and sparse-oracle interfaces retain explicit inverse/control access and projector-reflection unitarity.
Reversible arithmetic uses the exact control-preserving CNOT XOR action.
Coherent blocks require explicit availability; circuit inversion reverses chronology and takes separately available adjoints.
CNOT-based copying and uncomputation preserve wire order; phase-query control is not inferred from ordinary access.
Exact CNOT and controlled blocks retain scalar phases and the declared control-target order.
Controlled-phase approximation uses exact Pθ and CPθ; projective phase guarantees are not moved through controls.
Controlled T is diag(I2,T), and synthesis distinguishes exact equality from scalar-phase equivalence.
CNOT Pauli action uses the first control wire and exact controlled-X block.
Bell preparation and decoding use control-first CNOT and the reverse gate order.
Syndrome extraction cites CNOT with data as control and ancilla as XOR target.
Embedded CZ gates use CP(π)=diag(1,1,1,−1); CNOT routing preserves ordered-wire conventions.
The ideal gate-family model explicitly grants controlled Ry and uses control-first blocks with separately stated costs.
